calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Flyers’ net
calls.body: The Sabres have been around the middle of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Flyers one of the worst. Expect the Sabres to spend more of the night in the Flyers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.
calls.call: The Sabres get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

surprises.head: Dan Vladař stole one
surprises.body: Vladař allowed 1 goal on 28 shots, worth 3.5 expected goals: 2.5 fewer than expected. That is more than Philadelphia’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 30 starts.

story.head: Knuble scores his first two NHL goals as the Flyers beat the Sabres
paras: Cole Knuble, in his second NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Oliver Bonk, midway through the first to open the scoring for the Flyers. Trevor Zegras made it 2-0 on the power play four and a half minutes later, and that one stood up as the winner. Jason Zucker got the Sabres on the board on the power play late in the second, in his first game of the season. Knuble scored his second NHL goal early in the third to make it 3-1 for the Flyers. Hunter McDonald and Mattias Samuelsson dropped the gloves late in the period.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Dan Vladař made 27 saves for the Flyers, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 23 of 26 at the other end.

Samuelsson was thrown out with a game misconduct late in the third. The Sabres killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a little over a minute late in the second. The Flyers moved to 3-6-3 and climbed to sixth in the Metropolitan, while the Sabres fell to 4-4-2, slipping to seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Flyers.
Jack Quinn extended his point streak against Philadelphia to six games.
Michael Bunting was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Tyson Foerster played instead.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
